name: Korrath Yuzu-Ginger Stim Chews
description: Dense, chewy rectangles infused with yuzu oil and crystallized synth-ginger, carrying a measured nootropic-stimulant load designed for two to four hours of mild focus enhancement. Individually wrapped in heat-sealed foil.
flavor_profile: Bright yuzu citrus with a warm ginger bite, mildly astringent, and a clean 'lift' sensation that kicks in within eight minutes
cultural_context: Positioned as a premium alternative to stim-tabs for Tier 3 professionals who consider pharmaceutical stimulants too clinical. Korrath markets aggressively to BCI-augmented users, claiming the formula pairs well with focus-mode BCI states — a claim that is legally unverified but widely repeated.
story_hooks: A Korrath Biosweets researcher approaches the party claiming the nootropic compound in the chews has an undocumented interaction with certain military-grade BCI implants — causing brief, involuntary memory access in augmented users.

The Tier 4 market for Korrath Chews has created a counterfeit problem: street-level fakes look identical but carry a much heavier stim load, and three hospitalization cases have been quietly buried by a distributor.

A Tier 3 study group has been microdosing multiple Korrath Chews daily for months; one member has developed an unusual cognitive pattern that a corporate neuroscience team wants to study — without the subject's knowledge.
